title: Reorder reminders for repeat customers

problem.text: Many first-time buyers never place a second order; post-first-purchase retention is weak
problem.quote: most first-time buyers never come back for a second order

problem.text: Customers who loved a wine forget to come back and reorder it

why_now.text: Retention is a current team priority
why_now.quote: The reason I pulled this group together is retention

why_now.text: Lifecycle recently quantified the drop-off, creating urgency

success_looks_like.text: Convert one-time buyers into repeat buyers (more second orders)

translation.problem_statement: Nudge customers who bought an everyday wine they liked to reorder it before they run out, converting one-time buyers into repeat buyers — without over-emailing them.

requirements.text: Send an email reminder ~30 days after purchase to reorder favorites
requirements.underlying_need: A timely nudge to reorder a wine the customer is likely running low on

requirements.text: Let customers set up an auto-shipped subscription for a wine
Personalize reminder timing from each customer's purchase history
Only nudge on repeat-friendly 'everyday' wines, excluding occasion/gift buys
Protect customers from email over-frequency relative to existing campaigns

assumptions.text: The 30-day reorder window is a guess, not validated
Email is the v1 channel (vs push/SMS)
A category-level cadence heuristic is the realistic start this quarter; per-customer model is later

in_scope.text: Braze email nudging repeat-friendly customers to reorder favorites
Category-level timing heuristic (shorter for everyday, longer for premium)
Targeting limited to lower-price wines bought in quantity > 1

out_of_scope.quote: keep that out of scope for v1

out_of_scope.text: New messaging vendor; SMS pending legal consent review

open_decisions.text: Whether 30 days is the right default timing
Who owns the feature — lifecycle campaign vs engineering-built product (possibly hybrid)
Channels beyond email (push/SMS) deferred pending consent + capacity

functional.text: Identify customers eligible for a reorder nudge from prior purchases
Select eligible products (everyday, lower-price, qty>1; exclude occasion/gift)
Trigger a Braze email at a category-derived interval after purchase

non_functional.text: Needs order-history access to decide what/when to remind
Must not email on occasion/gift purchases (bad-experience guardrail)
Frequency cap across all Braze campaigns to prevent over-emailing
SMS would require legal sign-off on consent

dependencies.text: Global Braze frequency cap does not exist yet and may be a hard prerequisite
A signal distinguishing 'everyday repeat' from 'occasion' buys (not available today; must approximate)

risks.description: Email fatigue → unsubscribes and degraded deliverability that takes months to recover
Wrong reorder timing (wine cadence varies widely) annoys customers
Reminding on gift/occasion purchases creates bad experiences

technical.approach_sketch: v1: a Braze-triggered email to customers with a qualifying repeat-friendly purchase, timed by a category-level heuristic, gated behind a global frequency cap, excluding occasion buys. Per-customer cadence modelling and extra channels deferred. Eng not to start until the frequency-cap dependency is resolved.

gaps.why_it_matters: No defined metric or target (second orders? repeat revenue?) means the team can't agree later whether it worked, or size the investment.
Unclear whether lifecycle marketing or engineering owns it; blocks staffing and the build-vs-campaign decision.
The 30-day default is admittedly a guess; wrong timing is a primary driver of the annoyance risk.
No clean signal exists to exclude gift/occasion buys, yet that exclusion is a core guardrail.
A global cap doesn't exist and may be large; if it's a hard prerequisite it sets the timeline.
Ambiguous whether this targets all repeat-friendly buyers or a subset (e.g., wine club); changes audience size and design.

clarifying_questions.question: What is the success metric and target (e.g., second-order rate or repeat revenue over what window), and what holdout measures it?
Is the global Braze frequency cap a hard prerequisite for launch, and who scopes and owns building it?
Who owns this feature end to end — lifecycle marketing, engineering, or a defined hybrid?
What data can distinguish everyday repeat wines from occasion/gift purchases today, and how accurate must the v1 approximation be?
What is the initial category timing heuristic (which categories, which windows) and how will we validate it against real reorder intervals?
Which customers are in the v1 audience — all qualifying repeat buyers or a narrower segment such as wine club?

readiness_rationale: A clear problem and a sensible v1 shape exist, but launch is blocked on an undefined success metric, unresolved ownership, and a possibly-large frequency-cap prerequisite.
